title: Book One · Chapter 131: A Month on Paper
story:
The second talk about the table happens after supper. Ronan is in the yard with his book. He can hear Mr Qiu and Mrs Lan through the open front door.

He tries to read. He reads the same short line again. He is listening for news about the table.

“You can go in,” Mum says. “Ask them, “May I sit with you?””

Ronan knocks on the door. Mrs Lan looks up.

“Can the table stay? I want to know.”

“So do we,” she says. “Sit down.”

He sits near the doorway. The adults have tea. There is no cup for him yet. Mr Qiu moves the sugar bowl away from Ronan. “Would you like some water?” he asks Ronan.

Ronan nods.

Mrs Lan begins with the path. It has stayed clear. The table is empty at supper time. The small boxes fit on the high shelf. Her front room is her own again.

“But the side door must be locked at night,” she says.

Mr Qiu agrees. “I can bring the key back before supper.”

“And I have thought about the payment.”

Ronan looks at his water. He does not ask the price. Mrs Lan tells Mr Qiu her price. He listens, then asks for a lower price. He will not use the table all day. He explains that to her.

They talk for a while. No one gets angry. No one says yes at once either.

Mum comes to the door. “I am taking the washing in. Do you need me?”

“For a moment,” Mrs Lan says.

She asks Mum about the way to the kitchen. Does the table make it hard to get through? Mum says the clear line helps. But there must not be more stock along the wall.

“There won't be,” Mr Qiu says.

“That means on busy days too,” Mum adds.

He nods. They agree on a small payment and another month. After that they can talk again. The old stall may not be ready soon. Mr Qiu has decided not to wait beside a closed shutter every morning.

Ronan lets out a long breath.

Mrs Lan hears him.

“You have been very quiet. Were you worried?”

“I thought you might say no.”

“I might have.”

He looks at Mr Qiu. The old man drinks his tea and sets the cup down.

“Then I would need another plan.”

Ronan does not like that answer very much. He likes the table being there. He likes seeing the old board with Mr Qiu's name on it from the street.

But Mr Qiu is smiling. He takes a little notebook from his pocket. He writes the last day of this month in it. Mrs Lan checks it. Both write their names.

“May I leave the table here at night?” Mr Qiu asks. Mrs Lan walks to the gate and looks at the clear path one more time.

“With nothing on top,” she says.

“Nothing.”

“And a cloth over it when the rain blows in.”

Mr Qiu writes that down too. Ronan looks at the two names at the bottom. Mr Qiu and Mrs Lan have both agreed. Both have written their names to show that. Mrs Lan puts her copy in a drawer. Mr Qiu folds his and keeps it inside the little notebook, away from his coins.

Ronan takes his empty cup to the kitchen. Mum is there with the washing basket.

“A month,” he tells her.

“I heard.”

He picks up his book again. He finds his last line and starts there. This time he gets to the next page before anyone calls his name.

---

重点表达：payment＝使用费；another month＝再一个月；lets out a long breath＝长长呼出一口气。

情节提示：shutter＝店铺卷帘；drawer＝抽屉；locked＝锁好的。

理解：1. 延长摆摊安排需要满足什么条件？2. Mr Qiu 如果不能留下，打算怎样做？
